subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains how to read issue trackers to identify task scope, priority labels, and the relationship between issues and pull requests.
key_points: Read acceptance criteria to determine the exact scope of work.
Priority determines when to act; Severity determines impact level.
Always link PRs to issues for traceability.
misconceptions: Reading only the issue title is enough to understand the task.
Severity and Priority mean the same thing.
It is fine to start work when acceptance criteria are vague.
check_questions: What is the most important element in an issue description?
What is the difference between Priority and Severity?
What should you do first when acceptance criteria are missing?

fact_candidates: Standard components of an issue (title, description, labels, milestone, assignee)
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding whether to start work when acceptance criteria are ambiguous
error_interpretation_candidates: Identifying missing information in an incomplete issue report
scenario_candidates: Bug issue with no acceptance criteria and P1 label
Feature issue with clear acceptance criteria and P2 label
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Confusing Severity with Priority when deciding work order
Assuming the issue title alone defines the full scope
